newsitem.title: USA: Idaho attorney general sues tobacco industry.
newsitem.headline: Idaho attorney general sues tobacco industry.

text.p: Idaho's attorney general sued the tobacco industry to recoup public health-care costs related to smoking, his office said on Tuesday.
Attorney General Al Lance's lawsuit was filed in the Fourth District Court in Boise against Philip Morris Cos Inc and several other tobacco companies, his office said.
The names of the other defendants and details about the Idaho lawsuit were not immediately available.
In a statement dated June 9, Lance said his lawsuit was similar to those filed by other states.
"I want to stop the tobacco industry from targeting our children and end its efforts to induce our children to start smoking," Lance said in the statement.
Lance said his goal was also to stop the "misrepresentations that the industry has made about its products" and recover the state's smoking-related expenses.
Lance declined further comment on the lawsuit "because of the nature of this litigation." His spokesman was not immediately available to comment.

Earlier on Tuesday, the state of Oregon filed suit against the tobacco industry, bringing to 36 the number of states seeking restitution for health care spending allegedly related to illness caused by smoking.

Companies named as defendants in the Oregon lawsuit are Philip Morris Cos Inc.; R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.; Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp., its parent company, B.A.T Industries Plc, and two former subsidiaries; United States Tobacco Co., a unit of UST Inc.; and Lorillard Tobacco Co., a unit of Loews Corp.
Also named are industry trade groups and representatives Hill & Knowlton Inc., The Council for Tobacco Research - U.S.A. Inc., Smokeless Tobacco Council Inc. and Tobacco Institute Inc.
